subject: horse
name: Leading & Halter Response
summary: The horse's ability to yield politely to light halter requests and lead calmly beside a handler.
purpose: Forms the foundation for safe daily handling, veterinary/farrier care, and groundwork.
safety: Introduce halter requests progressively in an enclosed space before working near distractions.

introductory.overview: Yielding to light halter requests (forward, halt, step back, turn) and leading politely at walk on a loose line in familiar spaces.

components.title: Halter softness
components.description: Stepping forward, halting, backing, and turning lightly without leaning, pulling, or crowding.

components.title: Polite walk leading
components.description: Matching the handler's pace calmly without forging ahead or lagging.

introductory.learning: Leads and yields to the halter in familiar settings with occasional pushing, lagging, or distraction.
introductory.proficient: Calmly and reliably yields to light halter requests and leads politely at walk on a relaxed lead without crowding, pulling, or bolting.

intermediate.overview: Leading politely at walk and trot, turning cleanly, and staying attentive in busier or unfamiliar environments.

components.title: Trot-up and distractions
components.description: Trotting beside the handler on a light lead, halting promptly, and maintaining manners around other horses or activity.

intermediate.learning: Leads at trot or in busier spaces with intermittent tension or surging.
intermediate.proficient: Consistently leads calmly at walk and trot on a light lead, halts and backs promptly, and maintains respectful personal space in varied environments.

subject: horse
name: Standing Quietly
summary: The horse's ability to stand calmly and patiently when tied, held, or asked to wait in place.
purpose: Keeps the horse safe and relaxed during grooming, tacking, waiting at trailers, and farrier or vet visits.
safety: Always use safe tie points and breakaway/quick-release arrangements; never ground-tie near traffic or unenclosed hazards.

introductory.overview: Standing calmly when tied in a familiar, quiet location for routine care.

components.title: Tied patience
components.description: Standing without pulling back, pawing, or crowding when tied safely in a familiar spot.

introductory.learning: Stands tied for short periods with occasional fidgeting, pawing, or mild tension.
introductory.proficient: Stands quietly and relaxed when tied in familiar settings for routine grooming and preparation without pulling back or fussing.

intermediate.overview: Standing calmly when tied in busier environments, at trailers, or when nearby horses move away.

components.title: Patience around distractions
components.description: Maintaining composure when herd mates leave or activity occurs nearby.

intermediate.learning: Stands tied around mild distractions with intermittent restlessness.
intermediate.proficient: Stands calmly and reliably when tied in varied or busier locations—including trailers and group settings—without panicking or pulling back.

advanced.overview: Reliable ground-tying (standing in place with lead dropped or slack) in appropriate enclosed or controlled settings.

components.title: Ground-tie discipline
components.description: Waiting calmly in place while the handler steps away briefly and moves around.

advanced.learning: Holds position with lead dropped for brief moments in quiet spaces before wandering.
advanced.proficient: Reliably remains standing calmly in place on a dropped lead while the handler steps away and returns, without wandering or grazing.

subject: horse
name: Daily Care Handling
summary: The horse's calm cooperation during routine care—grooming, blanketing, bathing, and tacking up.
purpose: Reduces stress and injury risk during everyday care and preparation.
safety: Build comfort gradually with sensitive horses; never force acceptance through restraint alone.

introductory.overview: Standing calmly and accepting routine grooming, blanketing, bathing, and saddling/bridling in familiar settings.

components.title: Grooming and blanketing
components.description: Accepting brushes, blankets, and straps around legs/belly calmly.

components.title: Bathing and tacking
components.description: Accepting water/hosing and saddle/bridle placement without pinning ears, kicking, or evading.

introductory.learning: Accepts daily care and tacking with mild fidgeting or sensitivity around girth, ears, or water.
introductory.proficient: Cooperates calmly and stands quietly for routine grooming, blanketing, bathing, and saddling/bridling without bracing, biting, or kicking.

intermediate.overview: Remaining relaxed during full-body bathing, clippers/sprays, and tacking in unfamiliar or busier venues.

components.title: Confidence in varied settings
components.description: Maintaining calm cooperation at clinics, shows, wash stalls, or around unfamiliar gear.

intermediate.learning: Cooperates with sprays, clippers, or busy wash areas with occasional tension.
intermediate.proficient: Remains relaxed and cooperative during thorough bathing, grooming, blanketing, and tacking even in busy or unfamiliar environments.

subject: horse
name: Hoof Handling
summary: The horse's ability to yield all four hooves willingly, balance calmly, and cooperate for hoof cleaning and farrier care.
purpose: Essential for safe daily hoof maintenance and stress-free trimming or shoeing.
safety: Respect the horse's balance and physical comfort, especially in older or stiff horses.

introductory.overview: Lifting all four hooves willingly on light request and holding them calmly for routine hoof picking.

components.title: Yielding and holding
components.description: Shifting weight smoothly and holding each hoof briefly without snatching away or leaning heavily.

introductory.learning: Picks up feet with hesitation, mild leaning, or snatching back before being released.
introductory.proficient: Willingly lifts all four hooves on light request, balances comfortably, and holds each foot calmly for thorough cleaning.

intermediate.overview: Standing patiently for extended farrier work (trimming, rasping, or shoeing) on all four limbs.

components.title: Farrier patience
components.description: Accepting hoof stands, rasping, and longer holding intervals calmly without pulling.

intermediate.learning: Cooperates with farrier work for short intervals before becoming restless.
intermediate.proficient: Stands calmly and cooperatively through complete trimming or shoeing sessions on all four hooves.

subject: horse
name: Veterinary & Medical Handling
summary: The horse's calm cooperation during health checks, vital-sign measurement, oral medication, and routine veterinary examinations.
purpose: Allows accurate vital signs, safe treatment, and calmer emergency care.
safety: Prepare horses gradually with positive, low-stress practice rather than waiting for an emergency.

intermediate.overview: Standing quietly for physical exams, stethoscope, thermometer, mouth/eye checks, and oral medication.

components.title: Cooperative exam behavior
components.description: Accepting unfamiliar handlers, palpation, vital-sign checks, and oral syringes calmly.

intermediate.learning: Tolerates routine exam steps with mild tension or head-shyness.
intermediate.proficient: Stands calmly and cooperatively for physical exams, temperature/pulse/respiration checks, and oral administration without panicking or evading.

subject: horse
name: Trailer Loading
summary: The horse's willingness to walk calmly into a trailer, wait quietly while secured, and unload smoothly without rushing.
purpose: Supports safe, low-stress transport for travel, outings, and emergencies.
safety: Allow time for calm inspection and never rush unloading backward or forward.

intermediate.overview: Loading willingly, standing calmly while butt bars/doors are closed, and unloading smoothly.

components.title: Calm entry and exit
components.description: Stepping onto the ramp or step-up calmly without bolting in or backing out abruptly.

intermediate.learning: Loads with brief hesitation or rushes slightly during loading or unloading.
intermediate.proficient: Steps calmly into the trailer on light request, stands quietly while secured, and unloads smoothly at a controlled walk.

subject: horse
name: Ground Driving
summary: The horse's learned ability to move forward, halt, and turn calmly in response to two long lines handled from behind or beside it.
purpose: Builds confidence, steering clarity, and forward acceptance without a rider's weight.
safety: Ensure the horse calmly accepts lines touching its sides and hindquarters before driving; early sessions require a handler proficient in Rider Ground Driving.

introductory.overview: Calmly accepting driving gear and lines along the body, walking forward, halting, and turning in an enclosed area.

components.title: Line acceptance
components.description: Remaining relaxed when two lines rest lightly against sides and quarters.

components.title: Walk, halt, and basic turns
components.description: Responding to light, steady requests without bracing, rushing, or turning to face the handler.

introductory.learning: Accepts lines with mild tension or hesitation; may need a helper at the head or show delayed halts/turns.
introductory.proficient: Calmly accepts equipment and lines touching its body, walks forward willingly, and halts and turns both ways in an enclosed area on light requests without bracing or rushing.

intermediate.overview: Moving forward confidently at walk and trot with steady rhythm, straightness, prompt transitions, and composure in varied settings.

components.title: Trot straightness and adaptability
components.description: Following figures and transitions smoothly at walk and trot and staying calm if lines brush legs unexpectedly.

intermediate.learning: Drives at trot or outside the arena with occasional rushing, bracing, or loss of straightness.
intermediate.proficient: Drives forward confidently at walk and trot with steady rhythm and straightness, makes prompt transitions, follows figures cleanly, and stays calm in varied settings.
